thread.title: Midday Update: Energy Sector Buoys Wall Street

author: MT Newswires
title: Midday Update: Energy Sector Buoys Wall Street
text:
Shutterstock photo Wall Street is building on Friday's rally with the energy and technology sector fueling a 200-point gain in the Dow Jones Industrial Average, and three-week high in the Nasdaq Composite.
Oil futures continued to gain ground Monday with geopolitical risks driving West Texas Intermediate crude oil futures to a 3.5-year high. While Saudi Arabia orchestrates a hike in oil prices to $80 per barrel, Venezuela faces a deepening economic crisis, and President Donald Trump considers whether the U.S. should end its participation in the Iranian nuclear deal before Saturday.
The technology sector was again propping up the major indices, led by a record high in shares of component stock Apple ( AAPL ) and strength in chipmakers. Apple shares were building on Friday's rally after Berkshire Hathaway's (BRK.A, BRK.B) Warren Buffet heaped more praise on the company.
European shares tracked their U.S. counterparts higher with the help of a weaker euro and gains in Nestle after the food conglomerate signed a deal to market Starbucks ( SBUX ) products globally.
Crude oil was up $0.81 to $70.53 per barrel. Natural gas was up $0.04 to $2.75 per 1 million BTU. Gold was unchanged at $1,314.70 an ounce, while silver was up $0.001 to $16.52 an ounce. Copper was up $0.005 to $3.09 per pound.
Among energy ETFs, the United States Oil Fund was up 1.28% to $14.27 with the United States Natural Gas Fund was up 1.24% to $22.42. Amongst precious-metal funds, the Market Vectors Gold Miners ETF was up 0.37% to 22.73 while SPDR Gold Shares were up 0.02% to $124.57. The iShares Silver Trust was down 0.03% to $15.53.
